solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Soldier, one in the main near a Queen

parts.note: the main is the sea, and huss is a fish found there, the dogfish sold under that name
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A sailor-soldier stands at sea beside a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' just places the pieces side by side. Huss is the fishmonger's name for dogfish, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a light cavalryman, a kind of mounted trooper.

clue.text: Raise one to enter the army

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a host is an army, as in the heavenly host
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An order to lift a recruit into the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to lift up or raise, often with ropes.

clue.text: Kindle containing first for reader's support

indicators.note: the first word holds the extra letter inside it

parts.note: to stir up a feeling is to kindle it

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word reader is taken

explanation.surface: An e-reader device with something to help the person reading it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kindle' looks like the e-reader brand but means arouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup supports a rider's foot when mounted on a horse.

clue.text: Barrage of hot rock set up an old rebel

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means the word is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: lava is molten rock
Che Guevara, the late revolutionary

explanation.surface: A volcano erupts over an aged revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche of things is a sudden overwhelming flood, like a barrage of questions.

clue.text: Long-lasting bread's first slice, not crisp outside

indicators.note: the first letter cuts its way into the other word like a knife slicing a loaf

parts.note: bread that is no longer crisp and fresh is stale

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word bread is taken

explanation.surface: A baker's note about stale bread that has gone soft on the crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' confirms that the word for not crisp sits round the inserted letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stable is enduring and steady, so it lasts a long time.

clue.text: Completely familiar shopping bags

definitions.meaning: an informal slang word for totally
large open bags used for carrying goods

explanation.surface: Someone knows their shopping bags inside out.
explanation.definitionFit: Totes is casual slang for totally and also means large carrier bags.

clue.text: Prohibit processed fuel — it's poisonous

parts.note: to prohibit is to ban

indicators.note: the word fuel is put through a process that changes its letters

explanation.surface: A campaign to outlaw refined fuel because it is toxic.
explanation.definitionFit: Baneful means harmful or deadly, like poison.

clue.text: To appear cold in New York could be a catastrophe

parts.note: to emerge is to come into view

indicators.note: the letter for cold is placed inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A cold snap arriving in Manhattan might be disastrous.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency is a crisis, a sudden serious situation needing action.

clue.text: Like something aluminium related to popular technology

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
it can mean an indefinite something, as in 'she has it'
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A description of something made of aluminium in modern gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Computer-based, electronic technology is described as digital, the everyday tech of today.

clue.text: Small mischevious child is a horror

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tinker is a British word for a naughty, mischief-making youngster

explanation.surface: A little rascal of a child is described as a terror.
explanation.definitionFit: A horror, like a stinker, is a nasty or very unpleasant person or thing.

clue.text: Stall in the street? You'll get rag here

definitions.text: Stall in the street? You'll get rag here

parts.words: Stall in the street? You'll get rag here
parts.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper, and a street kiosk sells papers

explanation.walkthrough: 'rag' looks like cloth but is slang for a tabloid paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A street kiosk selling newspapers and magazines is the place to buy a rag.

clue.text: Name those paying attention to visionaries

parts.note: a big name is a star, a celebrity
people who gaze at something are watching it closely

explanation.surface: An instruction to identify the people who listen to prophets.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamers who look ahead to the future are called stargazers, idealists with heads in the clouds.

clue.text: Cool people don't care for these fruit

definitions.text: Cool people don't care for these
definitions.meaning: relaxed folk who are unbothered 'don't give a fig' about things
the soft sweet fruit of the fig tree

explanation.surface: Trendy people turn their noses up at a certain fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'not care a fig' means not care at all, and figs are also a Mediterranean fruit.

clue.text: Jelly is so far still, perhaps

parts.note: 'so far as' and 'as far as' are equivalent, so the words so far stand for as
a still is a photograph, and pic is short for picture; 'perhaps' marks an example

explanation.surface: A jelly that has so far stayed unmoving.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: A gathering of Labour is high point for city

parts.note: a crop is a harvest, something gathered in
o' is a short form of of, as in will-o'-the-wisp
L is the abbreviation for the British Labour party

explanation.surface: A rally of a political party is the high point for a city.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is a citadel built on the highest ground of an ancient Greek town.

clue.text: Down with manufacturing facility — it's to topple

parts.note: to down a drink is to sup it
a factory is a plant

explanation.surface: A protest slogan against a factory that is to be knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplant is to oust or overthrow someone and take their place.

clue.text: Soldier on a grave

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds a head
grave means serious, severe

explanation.surface: A soldier standing on a grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier on' reads as a noun and preposition but is a phrasal verb meaning keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is to carry on doggedly despite difficulty.

clue.text: The future professionals loudly kissed

parts.note: pros is short for professionals

indicators.note: the word is spoken aloud, so a word sounding like it is used

parts.note: to peck is to kiss lightly, so kissed is pecked

explanation.surface: The coming days see experts kissing noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: PECT is not a word; it sounds like 'pecked'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is an outlook or expectation of what lies ahead.

clue.text: Doctor remains for conference

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician's body is the subject of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a meeting for discussion, a small academic conference.

clue.text: Capacious jumper, gosh!

parts.note: a kangaroo, roo for short, is a jumper
'my!' is an exclamation of surprise like gosh

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at how big a woolly sweater is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a British sweater but is the hopping animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy and capacious both mean spacious, with plenty of space inside.

clue.text: Trace absent ancestry

parts.note: someone who is out is away, not present
a line is a lineage, a family descent

explanation.surface: Trying to track down a missing family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace is to draw the outline of a shape.

clue.text: Vespa moped delivers junk food

indicators.note: the phrase gives up a run of letters found inside its words

explanation.surface: A scooter courier brings unhealthy takeaway food.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is a tinned processed pork product, a classic cheap convenience meat.

clue.text: Transformed inn merited an occasion to scoff

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A renovated pub earned a chance for mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoff' looks like mocking but is British slang for eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening meal hour is when one gets to eat heartily.

clue.text: Ideal d-drill

parts.note: to ream is to widen a hole with a drilling tool

explanation.walkthrough: The stutter 'd-' supplies a lone D before the word for drill.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is a perfect wish, something ideal one longs for.

clue.text: King dressed in kid's hat

indicators.note: the letter is clothed by the word around it

parts.note: a mite is a small child
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch wearing a child's headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is the tall pointed headdress worn by bishops.

clue.text: Place below rifle

parts.note: Pl is the abbreviation for place in street names
under means below

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a gun underneath something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a gun but is the verb meaning to ransack.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle through and to plunder both mean to ransack and steal from.

clue.text: I've turned into someone to take out stray

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a date is a person you take out for the evening

indicators.note: the letters of the word I've are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has become a stray who needs taking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I've turned into' reads as a confession of becoming someone, but 'turned' is the anagram signal and 'into' the container; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To deviate is to wander off course, to stray from the path.

clue.text: Pink and puny punk

definitions.meaning: a pale coral pink colour named after the crustacean
a small, feeble person, often a weedy youngster

explanation.surface: A description of a weak, pink-haired punk rocker.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimp is both a pinkish colour and an insult for a tiny weakling.

clue.text: Calm sneer upset English

indicators.note: the word sneer is knocked over and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An Englishman stays composed despite a disturbed sneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene and calm both mean peaceful and untroubled.
